answer: In PoA, trust propagates from honest seeds through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition mass attenuated at every hop. A sybil set’s sparse external cut has low conductance, limiting inflow; min-cut transitivity therefore bounds its reachable mass and aggregate voting weight, even when internal edges are dense. Basalt-like identity anchors strengthen attestations, nectar incentives are discounted, and a nadir threshold caps concentration.
